compatibility.bpStudio: Box-pleated design, flap packing, and its stretch and river devices.
compatibility.flatFolder: Jason S. Ku's flat-foldability checking and layer ordering.
compatibility.formats: Opens and exports .cp, .fold, .ori, .orh, .tmd5 and .bps, so nothing you make here is trapped here.
compatibility.lead: Much of Ori Studio is a careful port of work the origami community already built, and staying compatible with it is a priority rather than an afterthought.
compatibility.oriedita: The crease-pattern editor, and the bulk of what Ori Studio does.
compatibility.title: Built on the tools you already use
compatibility.treemaker: Robert J. Lang's solver for turning a tree structure into a crease pattern.

desktopOnly.body: Drawing a crease pattern, dragging a tree into shape and folding the result all want a mouse, a keyboard, and room to work. None of that fits a phone yet, so this is not going to pretend otherwise.
desktopOnly.invitation: Open this page on a computer and the whole thing is there. In the meantime, here is what it does.
desktopOnly.openAnywayNote: It will be cramped, and the tools that need a hover or a right-click have no touch equivalent yet.
desktopOnly.title: Desktop only, for now

get.lead: The web app is the whole thing — no account, and your files stay on your machine unless you choose to share one. The desktop build adds native menus, file dialogs, and opening files from Finder.
get.note: Signed Apple Silicon builds today; other platforms are coming, and help with them is welcome.
get.title: Run it in the browser, or install it

what.lead: Ori Studio brings the tools origami designers already use into a single place. Sketch a tree structure and let it find a base, draw and edit the crease pattern by hand, then fold it in the simulator to see what you made — without exporting between four programs to do it.
what.title: One workspace, from tree to folded model

design.body: Start from a tree structure and let the optimizer pack circles into a base, or lay flaps out on a box-pleating grid. Both hand you a crease pattern you can keep working on.
design.title: Design

edit.body: A full crease-pattern editor: draw, fold and unfold, check flat-foldability, and keep a reference photo of the subject beside the paper. It can also read a crease pattern straight out of an image.
edit.title: Edit

simulate.body: Fold the pattern and turn it over. The simulator runs on the crease pattern you are editing, so trying an idea never means leaving the document.
simulate.title: Simulate
